A common weather pattern you might see is a cold front. Imagine a big wall of cold air moving in from up north. This cold air is heavier than the warm air it's replacing, so it pushes the warm air up and out of the way. As the warm air rises, it cools and forms clouds, which can then turn into rain or thunderstorms.
